## Decisions
- Creative LUT is a **distinct effect type** (`builtin.lut.creative`) from the tier-1 `builtin.colortransform`, per ARCHITECTURE §18's explicit tier separation — never merge them, never let a look carry the tier-1 transform (enforced in `LookRules.IsLookEffect`, `LookApplication.Build` skip logic, AND `LooksStore.Deserialize`'s strip-with-warning, i.e. defense in depth at 3 layers).
- Looks are **app-wide** (stored in `%AppData%/Sprocket/looks.json`), **not per-project** and **not undo-tracked** — matches Premiere's Lumetri presets / Resolve's PowerGrade album mental model. Applying a look to a clip IS undoable (ordinary `CompositeCommand`); saving/renaming/deleting a look is NOT undoable via the project's `EditHistory` (confirmed via `ConfirmDialog` before delete instead).
- `LookApplication.Build` always **appends** a look's effects to the end of the clip's stack (after any existing tier-1 transform and any prior grading), never inserts at a fixed index — mirrors how a colourist stacks corrections, and keeps the "apply a second look on top" workflow intact (undo to try another).
- Values in `LookEntry.Values`/`Assets` that fail validation (NaN, undeclared param name, out-of-range) are clamped/dropped rather than throwing — matches the existing "degrade, never crash" convention (§15) used throughout the codebase (e.g. `ColorLuts.TryGet`, `ImpulseResponseCache`).
- `CreativeLuts` loads **synchronously on first use** (not backgrounded like `ImpulseResponseCache`) specifically so export's first frame doesn't miss the look — `Preload()` exists as an explicit off-thread warm-up the App layer calls after applying a look, so the *UI* path stays non-blocking while *render/export* stays deterministic.
- MCP `add_effect` tool was **not extended** to know about looks in this session — open question whether Phase 3 should add an `apply_look` MCP tool (mirroring `add_effect`'s preset param) or whether that's out of scope / a follow-up. Not decided yet — the SprocketTools.cs review only happened at exploration time, no code written there.
- The visual look-tuning contact-sheet harness (`ZzLookSheetTmp.cs`) was a deliberate throwaway (test filename prefixed `Zz` to sort last / signal "temporary"), NOT meant to ship — explicitly noted for deletion before final commit.
